sb_prompt: WHAT DO YOU THINK ABOUT CURRENT OR RECENT AMERICAN ACTIONS IN LATIN AMERICA
turns: Yeah, honestly? The way the US is basically treating the whole region right now just feels really off to me. Like, we're supposed to be allies, but half the time it feels like we're just trying to break things up. I actually had a weird experience with this a few months ago when I was working in Miami. A guy who looked like he was from Central America was having a really bad night at my table, you know? Just crying about how hard it is to send money home, and honestly I was sympathetic, but then this other guy in a suit walked by and just started talking trash about the guy and how he was a criminal or something. It made me realize how much of that attitude just comes from where we are in the US. I feel like we're scared of our own neighbors. What about you? Did you ever go down there, or do you have an opinion on why the US is doing what they're doing?

I never even went down there, but honestly, that story hits way too close to home for me. Like, I've been doing plumbing for fifteen years and never once had a client talk trash about me just because of where I'm from or how I look. It feels like a lot of folks here in the US just get defensive if things don't go their way. So when you tell me someone was crying about sending money home and got called a criminal right after, it sounds familiar, even if the job is totally different.

Yeah, exactly, it's like the whole vibe is just "us versus them" even when they're literally right here in our city, and honestly I'm just tired of being the bridge for people who are actually trying to be good.

Yeah, it's that same feeling of people here thinking they know better than everyone else, even when they're just trying to help. It was just a total mess of misunderstanding, but it made me realize that once you're in a position where you can actually fix problems for people, you can't really stay mad at them for being scared.
